text:
Maya (CEO): Opening a rapid follow-up thread from today's all-hands — short Qs only. I'll answer or assign.

Marco (Sales): Need a one-liner that contrasts us vs 'model-first' vendors for enterprise decks.

Maya (CEO): Try: 'We make models production-ready: consistent SLAs, cost controls, and private deployments.' Keep it snappy.

Priya (Head of Product): Is prioritization still: 1) runtime latency, 2) rollout tooling, 3) cost UX?

Jon (CTO): Yes, with nuance: runtime work unlocks higher tiers; rollout tooling increases PLG conversion. Triage by active revenue impact.

Zoe (Customer Success): Field note — prospects ask about governance (audit + KMS). Do we have a short checklist to send?

Maya (CEO): Yes — send: 1) VPC/private control plane, 2) KMS/HSM integration, 3) audit logs + retention policy, 4) SLA options. Priya will add details.

Aiden (Eng): Quick tech snippet for demos showing graceful fallback?

Jon (CTO): Pasteable example:
```
route_policy:
  priority: [low_latency, cost]
  fallback: quantized_small
  canary: 10%
```
Explains behavior without deep infra.

DevBot: All-hands slides uploaded: https://redwood.internal/all-hands/mar-2026/slides.pdf

Marco (Sales): Can marketing share approved performance ranges for decks?

Priya (Head of Product): We'll publish conservative ranges (median latency and cost bands) after legal review — expect a short list by Friday.

Maya (CEO): Action items: Priya to publish metrics list, Jon to hand sales the YAML snippets, Zoe to collect governance checklist details. I'll follow up if any blockers. Thanks — keep additional Qs brief here. :raised_hands:
